candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Luke, Homily CXI (R. Payne Smith trans., 1859). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On the master's commendation of the unjust steward — 'the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely' (Lk 16:8) — Cyril reads the lord-commended-the-unjust paradox as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine that prudent-shrewdness in temporal matters should be matched by prudent-shrewdness in eternal matters: the steward is praised not for his dishonesty but for his foresight in securing his future. Tewahedo stewardship theology cites Lk 16:8 + Lk 16:9 ('make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness') as the canonical doubled-witness for the doctrine of strategic-almsgiving — the prudent Christian uses temporal wealth to build eternal friendships (the recipients of the alms welcome the giver into eternal habitations).
